  Digital System Design and Computer Organization [ECM_2122]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                    Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Design a combinational circuit using programmable logic array (PLA) to implement a full subtractor. (4)  
  
  
  A)                                                       Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Construct a Mod-10 ripple up-counter using negative edge triggered T flip-flops and draw the output (3)  
  timing diagrams.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)           Write Verilog dataflow code to implement 8:1 multiplexer without using the instances of 2:1           (3)  
  multiplexers.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2)                Design a 3-bit self-correcting synchronous counter using JK flip-flops that follows the sequence 7-6- (5)  
  4-3 repeatedly, ensuring that any unused states automatically go to the state-7 on the next clock  
  A)           pulse.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"

  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  C)           With an example, explain the role of instances in Verilog programming.                                (2)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
3)                Design a Mealy synchronous sequential circuit using D flip-flops with a serial input x and output z   (5)  
  that produces z = 1 whenever the input completes the sequence 1011. Overlapping is allowed.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Use the Booth's algorithm to multiply +23 (multiplicand) by -10 (multiplier), where each number is    (3)  
  represented using 6 bits.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)           Write a behavioral Verilog code for a 4:1 MUX using an "always block" and "case statement".           (2)

Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"

  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)         What is the difference between non-pipelined and pipelined processors? If the number of stages is (2)

  A)
